item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: BYON (Bring Your Own NIC) in Azure Site Recovery
item.description:
Azure Site Recovery now supports Bring Your Own NIC (BYON) for Azure-to-Azure test failover and failover, allowing you to attach an existing pre-provisioned NIC in the target region. This can preserve existing network configurations and reserved IP settings.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: dotnet: Routing and Failover for Microsoft.Extensions.AI
item.description:
Microsoft.Extensions.AI adds experimental routing primitives for model/provider selection and failover: RoutingChatClient, SemanticRoutingChatClient, and FailoverChatClient. These support content-based routing, failover handling, and custom routing policies.

  • Source: .NET

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Graceful failover with zero data loss guarantee
item.description:
Azure DocumentDB now generally available supports graceful failover that promotes replica clusters with a zero data loss guarantee. It is an addition to the existing force promote option, which promotes immediately.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Per-partition automatic failover for Azure Cosmos DB
item.description:
Per-partition automatic failover (PPAF) is now generally available in Azure Cosmos DB. It allows failover at the partition level instead of failing over an entire account during a regional disruption, improving recovery time and availability.

  • Source: Azure Updates

item.title: azure: [Launched] Generally Available: Service-managed failover in Azure DocumentDB
item.description:
Azure DocumentDB service-managed failover for multi-region clusters is now generally available. In a regional outage, Azure DocumentDB automatically fails over the globally distributed cluster from the primary region to another region.

  • Source: Azure Updates
